title: Hearty Syrian Semolina Pilaf
description: A yeasty, molten one-pot dish that blends semolina with a shio-koji cure and fragrant spices for a sattvic-friendly lunch. The resulting pilaf is airy, flavorful, and comforting.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Stir in the semolina, toasting it lightly until it turns a pale golden color.
Pour in the vegetable broth and shio-koji, stirring until the mixture thickens slightly.
Season with cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt, then add the chopped apricots.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 12 minutes, or until the semolina is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat, fluff the pilaf with a fork, and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Serve warm, optionally garnishing with fresh herbs or a drizzle of olive oil.
